submission.justification: Absorber-F2 with 4mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.201% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. This represents a ~17% improvement over the second-best option (Absorber-F1 at 3.855%) and ~36% improvement over Absorber-F3 (4.986%). The 4mm thickness provides optimal performance, with both thinner (2mm: 3.798%) and thicker plates (6mm: 3.201%, 8mm: 3.932%, 10mm: 4.556%) showing degraded resolution. CRITICAL CAVEAT: No dose rate data was available in the simulation results or project documents to verify compliance with the hard constraint of <20 uSv/h at 1m after one week cooldown. This safety requirement must be verified through additional radiation transport simulations or experimental measurements before final implementation, as it is essential for hands-on maintenance capability.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 4mm achieves 3.201% resolution, which is the best performance among all materials (F1: 3.855%, F3: 4.986%) and all tested thicknesses (2mm to 10mm range).

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is one of the three candidate materials (F1, F2, F3) evaluated in the study.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h for hands-on maintenance (HARD requirement)
requirements.evidence: No dose rate data was available in the simulation results (dose_rate_data_available = 0, all materials show F*_passes_constraint = -1). This critical safety constraint cannot be verified and requires additional radiation transport calculations before implementation.
Recommended thickness of 4mm is within the specified range of 2-10mm and was tested in the simulation campaign.
